Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Work & responsibility

available adjective

of a person: free, not busy

also free, not busy, have time, are you free?, at your disposal, if you are free, there is no time to (study)

classical

Cic. Att. 12.38.2: sīc scrībēs aliquid sī vacābis
Cic. Fam. 12.30.1: sī nē tū quidem vacās
Hor. Ep. 2.2.95: sī forte vacās (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 98: sī vacābis

vacō, vacāre, vacāvī, vacātum

verb, first conjugation; with a dative, “have time for”

be free, have time, be at leisure

Philosophiae semper vacō, “I always have time for philosophy” (Cic. Div. 1.10, Lewis & Short). The impersonal vacat with an infinitive, “there is time to”, is poetic and post-Augustan. The opposite is occupātus, busy.

Other words

  • ōtiōsus, ōtiōsa, ōtiōsum — at leisure, free, not busy

    also used · classical · Catull. 50.2: ōtiōsī multum lūsimus; Cic. Off. 3.1: numquam sē minus ōtiōsum esse quam cum ōtiōsus

  • praestō esse — be on hand, be at someone’s service

    with a dative of the person · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 19: praestō multīs fuit (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 4.1.4: ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō

Examples

  • tū, quoniam necesse nihil est, sīc scrībēs aliquid sī vacābis

    since there’s no need, just write a line if you have timeCic. Att. 12.38.2

  • aut, sī nē tū quidem vacās, nōlī impudēns esse

    or, if you aren’t free either, don’t be shamelessCic. Fam. 12.30.1

  • ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē

    my little Tullia was there to meet me, on her very birthdayCic. Att. 4.1.4

  • nōbīs vēnārī nec vacat nec libet

    I have neither the time nor the wish to huntPlin. Ep. 9.16.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nōn vacat studēre.

    There is no time to study.Traupman 109
